name: Brahmānanda Purī
text:
## In short

Brahmānanda Purī, a disciple of Mādhavendra Purī — one of the nine «roots» of the tree of devotion — who loved Nityānanda, took part in the Lord's kīrtana in Navadvīpa and was with Him in Nīlācala.

## Disciple of Mādhavendra Purī (Ādi 9.170)

> īśvara-purī brahmānanda-purī ādi yata
> sarva-śiṣya hailena nityānande rata

«Īśvara Purī, Brahmānanda Purī, and the other disciples of Mādhavendra Purī all felt great attachment for Lord Nityānanda.»

The *bhāṣya*: «Śrī Brahmānanda Purī was a disciple of Śrīman Mādhavendra Purī; in other words, he was one of the nine Nidhis or roots of the desire tree of devotional service (*Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 9.13). He was a participant in Śrī Mahāprabhu's saṅkīrtana pastimes in Navadvīpa. He also took part in Mahāprabhu's pastimes in Nīlācala.»

## A senior to the Lord (Ādi 12.248, bhāṣya)

The *bhāṣya* lists him among those who, by their relation, regarded the Lord as their junior: «in gaura-līlā, Brahmānanda Purī as a Godbrother of Īśvara Purī».

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 9.170; 12.248 (bhāṣya).

name: Jīva (Jīva Paṇḍita)
text:
## In short

Jīva Paṇḍita, son of Ratnagarbha Ācārya, «magnanimous and most fortunate»; Nityānanda enjoyed pastimes in his house.

## In the book

- **Son of Ratnagarbha** (Madhya 1.297), brother of Kṛṣṇānanda and Yadunātha Kavicandra.
- **Among Nityānanda's associates** (Antya 5.751):

> mahā-bhāgyavanta jīva paṇḍita udāra
> yāṅra ghare nityānanda-candrera vihāra

«The most fortunate Jīva Paṇḍita was magnanimous. Nityānanda Candra enjoyed pastimes in his house.»

The *bhāṣya* (Madhya 1.297): *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 11.44 says «Śrī Jīva Paṇḍita glorified the qualities of Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu»; according to the *Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā* (169) he was the Vrajavāsī **Indirā**.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 1.297 (with bhāṣya); Antya 5.751.

name: Paramānanda Upādhyāya
text:
## In short

Paramānanda Upādhyāya, of Nityānanda's company: «an unalloyed Vaiṣṇava».

## Among Nityānanda's associates (Antya 5.744)

> maheśa paṇḍita — ati parama mahānta
> paramānanda upādhyāya — vaiṣṇava ekānta

«Maheśa Paṇḍita was the most exalted devotee. Paramānanda Upādhyāya was an unalloyed Vaiṣṇava.» The *bhāṣya* refers to *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 11.44 and its *Anubhāṣya*.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Antya 5.744.

name: Ratnagarbha Ācārya
text:
## In short

Ratnagarbha Ācārya, a friend of the Lord's father from the same village, and a loving reciter of the *Bhāgavatam*: hearing him recite, the Lord fell to the ground in ecstasy and embraced him. Father of Kṛṣṇānanda, Jīva Paṇḍita and Yadunātha Kavicandra.

## His family (Madhya 1.295–297)

«He was well known by the name Ratnagarbha Ācārya, and he was a friend of the Lord's father, being born in the same village. His three sons — Kṛṣṇānanda, Jīva, and Yadunātha Kavicandra — were like bees at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.» The *bhāṣya*: Kṛṣṇānanda was one of Gaṅgādāsa Paṇḍita's main students, joined the water-sports after the deliverance of Jagāi and Mādhāi and was an associate of Nityānanda; Jīva Paṇḍita (Antya 5.751) and Yadunātha Kavicandra (Antya 5.735) too.

## The recitation (Madhya 1.298–312)

One night, as Viśvambhara explained the scriptures to His students, Ratnagarbha was sitting at the door of a nearby house — «that topmost brāhmaṇa had the highest respect for the *Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam*» — reciting the verse of the wives of the brāhmaṇas: «His complexion was dark blue and His garment golden. Wearing a peacock feather… He rested one hand upon the shoulder of a friend and with the other twirled a lotus» (*Bhāgavatam* 10.23.22).

«When the Lord heard that glorification of devotional service, He lost external consciousness and fell to the ground», and rolling on the ground cried «Go on reciting!» The brāhmaṇa recited with more devotion; the Lord embraced him. «Being embraced by the Lord of Vaikuṇṭha, Ratnagarbha became filled with love of God. Ratnagarbha wept aloud as he clasped the Lord's feet.» At last Gadādhara said, «Do not recite any more.»

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 1.293–312.

name: Śiva-bhakta brāhmaṇa
text:
## In short

A wandering singer of Śiva's glories who came begging to the Lord's door; the Lord, taking the mood of Śaṅkara, climbed on his shoulders.

## The singer of Śiva (Madhya 8.97–106)

«One day a singer of Śiva's glories arrived. He began to play his small drum and chant the glories of Lord Śiva. He came to the Lord's doorstep for begging alms and began to dance in a circle while singing a song about Lord Śiva.» As soon as Viśvambhara heard the qualities of Śaṅkara, He took the form of Śaṅkara with matted locks: «The Lord jumped on the shoulders of that singer and shouted loudly, “I am that Śaṅkara!”» Some saw Him with matted hair, playing a horn and *ḍamaru*, crying «Sing! Sing!»

«Whatever glorification of Śiva that great personality ever sang now bore its full fruits. Since that singer sang without offense, Gauracandra climbed on his shoulders.» Coming back to external consciousness, the Lord got down and put alms into the singer's bag with His own hands; fully satisfied, the singer left, and all the devotees chanted the names of Hari.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 8.97–106 (cf. *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 17.99–100).

name: Śrīgarbha
text:
## In short

Śrīgarbha (Śrīgarbha Paṇḍita), a close associate of the Lord in the Navadvīpa kīrtanas, named again and again in the *Caitanya-bhāgavata*.

## In the book

- **Invocations**: «All glories to the life and soul of Śrī Jagadānanda and Śrīgarbha!» (Madhya 7.3; 8.2); «All glories to the dear Lord of Vāsudeva and Śrīgarbha!» (Madhya 9.5).
- **Kīrtanas** in Śrīvāsa's house (Madhya 8.112–116) and after the deliverance of Jagāi and Mādhāi (Madhya 13.336–339).
- **The night before the Kazi** (Madhya 23.150–152): among the devotees expert in kīrtana who led the groups.
- **Weeping at the Lord's departure** (Madhya 23.451): «Govinda, Govindānanda, Śrīgarbha, Śrīmān, Kāśīśvara, Śrī Jagadānanda, and Rāma also began to cry.»
- **With Śacī-mātā** (Antya 4.273–274): with Haridāsa, Murāri, Nārāyaṇa, Jagadīśa and Gopīnātha, merged in ecstasy on seeing her satisfaction.
- **To Purī for the Ratha-yātrā** (Antya 8.26):

> gopīnātha paṇḍita āra śrīgarbha paṇḍita
> calilena dui kṛṣṇa-vigraha niścita

«Gopīnātha Paṇḍita and Śrīgarbha Paṇḍita, who were both certainly forms of Kṛṣṇa, also came.»

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 7.3, 8.2, 8.112–116, 9.5, 13.336–339, 23.150–152, 23.451; Antya 4.273–274, 8.26.

name: Sukhī (Duḥkhī, servant in Śrīvāsa's house)
text:
## In short

Duḥkhī, a maidservant in the house of Śrīvāsa, who brought Gaṅgā water for the Lord every day; the Lord renamed her **Sukhī**, «the happy one».

## The first time (Madhya 9.38–41)

At the Lord's great manifestation (*mahā-prakāśa*) the servants and maidservants of Śrīvāsa brought water to bathe Him. «One most fortunate maidservant named Duḥkhī brought water for the Lord, who encouraged her by saying, “Bring, bring.” On seeing her devotional service, the Lord changed her name from Duḥkhī to Sukhī.»

## The water-pots (Madhya 25.11–22)

«While the Lord was dancing in ecstasy, the pious Duḥkhī would bring water. Sometimes tears would come to her eyes as she watched the Lord dance, then she would go again and again to bring water from the Gaṅgā. She kept the waterpots in rows on all sides.» The Lord asked Śrīvāsa who brought the water every day. — «O Lord, Duḥkhī brings the water.» — «You should all call her Sukhī. The name Duḥkhī is not appropriate for her. I think she is always Sukhī.» The devotees wept for joy; «by the order of the Lord, everyone called her Sukhī, and from then on Śrīvāsa did not treat her as a maidservant.»

> «Despite being a maidservant, Duḥkhī received mercy that can never be seen by those who are falsely proud.» (Madhya 25.22)

The book draws the lesson: good birth, beauty, wealth and education are useless; Kṛṣṇa is pleased when He is served with love.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 9.38–41; 25.11–22.

name: Vallabhācārya
text:
## In short

Vallabhācārya (Vallabha Miśra), a poor but noble brāhmaṇa of Navadvīpa, «equal to King Janaka», father of Śrī Lakṣmīpriyā, the Lord's first wife.

## «Equal to Janaka» (Ādi 10.47)

> sei navadvīpe vaise eka subrāhmaṇa
> vallabha-ācārya nāma janakera sama

«There was one qualified brāhmaṇa in Navadvīpa named Vallabhācārya, who was equal to Janaka Mahārāja.» The *bhāṣya* quotes the *Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā* (44): Janaka, king of Mithilā, has appeared as Vallabhācārya; he is also Bhīṣmaka, father of Rukmiṇī — Jānakī, Rukmiṇī and Lakṣmī were all his daughters.

## The proposal (Ādi 10.55–78)

Vanamālī Ācārya described him to Śacī: «born in an exalted family… pure, well behaved, and decorated with many good qualities», his daughter «as good as Lakṣmī». When Vanamālī came with Śacī's consent, «Vallabha offered him a seat with great respect» and answered: «Such a husband for my daughter is achieved by great fortune. If Kṛṣṇa is pleased with me and Lakṣmī and Pārvatī are pleased with my daughter, then I will be blessed with such a husband for my daughter.» But, embarrassed: «I am poor and have no means to offer a dowry. I can offer only five *haritakī* fruits along with my daughter.»

## The wedding (Ādi 10.83–107)

He took part in the *adhivāsa* and worshipped the demigods and forefathers by the Vedic rules. At dusk the Lord came to his house, «and Vallabhācārya and his associates drowned in an ocean of bliss». He had his daughter brought before the Lord; then «Vallabhācārya, who is nondifferent from Bhīṣmaka, sat down to give away his daughter»: «the same lotus feet that are worshiped by Śaṅkara and Brahmā… were now worshiped by the respected brāhmaṇa Vallabhācārya», who decorated the Lord with cloth, garlands and sandalwood. The Lord stayed the night in his house and the next day returned home with Lakṣmī.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 10.47–107.

name: Yadu Kavicandra
text:
## In short

Yadunātha Kavicandra, youngest son of Ratnagarbha Ācārya, «full of the mellows of love for Kṛṣṇa», on whom Nityānanda always showered His mercy.

## In the book

- **Son of Ratnagarbha** (Madhya 1.297): «His three sons — Kṛṣṇānanda, Jīva, and Yadunātha Kavicandra — were like bees at the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.»
- **Among Nityānanda's associates** (Antya 5.735): «Yadunātha Kavicandra was filled with the mellows of ecstatic love. Nityānanda was always merciful to him.» The *bhāṣya* quotes *Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 11.35: «Yadunātha Kavicandra was a great devotee. Lord Nityānanda Prabhu always danced in his heart.»

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 1.297; Antya 5.735.

name: Brahmānanda (of the kīrtana at Navadvīpa)
text:
## In short

The Brahmānanda of the Navadvīpa kīrtanas, who played the old companion **Suprabhā** of Gadādhara in the Lord's drama. At the Lord's sannyāsa the book names «Brahmānanda Bhāratī» among the five who were present.

## In the kīrtanas (Madhya 8.112–116)

Named among the associates present every night at the kīrtanas in Śrīvāsa's house.

## In the drama (Madhya 18.102–108)

When Gadādhara came on stage as a gopī, «he happily wandered about with Brahmānanda, who accompanied Gadādhara in the role of his female companion Suprabhā. With a stick in one hand, a basket under the other arm, and dressed in fine cotton cloth, Brahmānanda looked just like an elderly lady.» Haridāsa called out: «Who are you?» — «We are going to Mathurā.» Śrīvāsa: «Who are your husbands?» — «Why are you asking?» Gaṅgādāsa: «Where will you stay today?» — «You will give us a place.»

## At the Lord's sannyāsa (Madhya 28.11–12, 103–104)

The Lord told Nityānanda the only five persons He could tell of His plan: «My mother, Gadādhara, Brahmānanda Bhāratī, Śrī Candraśekhara Ācārya, and Mukunda»; and these came to Kaṭwā. In Antya 2.40 the Lord asks «Nityānanda, Gadādhara, Mukunda, Govinda, and Brahmānanda» what assets they have — «We have no asset other than You.»

Whether this Brahmānanda is the same as Brahmānanda Bhāratī of Purī (#159) the book does not say plainly; it uses the name «Brahmānanda Bhāratī» here.

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 8.112–116; 18.102–108; 28.11–12, 28.103–104; Antya 2.40.

name: Puruṣottama (student of Lord Gaurāṅga)
replace:
(Caitanya Caritāmṛta 1.10.72, Caitanya Bhāgavata 1.15.5, 3.8.20)

The two places of the Caitanya-bhāgavata (Ādi 15.5, Antya 8.20) speak of **Puruṣottama Sañjaya**, son of Mukunda Sañjaya, «the Lord's principal student» — see #1138 and its text «In the Caitanya-bhāgavata» (16-11-2026).
